title: Tenant-weighted degradation profiles and error-budget escrow procedure for conversational routes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a tenant-weighted SLI/SLO binding and an error-budget escrow mechanism that enables progressive degradation profiles for conversational endpoints. This ticket covers specification, API surface for per-endpoint/model SLI declarations, escrow rules to borrow/repay error budget between regions and variants, circuit-breaker thresholds for tenant-prioritized shedding, and a runbook for safe rollout and rollback.

Background: We have multiple conversational routes with mixed latency/quality requirements and multi-tenant traffic. Current per-endpoint SLI work focuses on single-region allocations; we need a robust policy to: 1) bind SLIs to endpoint+model variants (latency p50/p95/p99, request success, quality prompts), 2) surface tenant weight (revenue or SLA tier) that influences degradation ordering, 3) escrow error-budget credits to allow temporary borrowing across regions/variants with automated repayment and reconciliation, and 4) define circuit-breaker and load-shedding behaviors that preserve high-priority tenant SLOs while avoiding global cascading failures.

Key concepts to capture: progressive degradation profiles (tiered latency/quality targets and graceful feature rollback), soft shedding (response truncation, cached prefix reuse, lower-cost quantized variant fallback), hard shedding (rejects with well-structured 429+Retry-After and debugging token), escrow ledger (per-tenant, per-endpoint: credits minted when under target, debited when borrowing), repayment policy (time-windowed payback with rate limits), KV-cache awareness (prefer cache hit preservation for high-priority tenants), and observability signals (per-tenant burn-rate, p99 latency shifts, model-quality regression tied to promptset evals).
acceptance_criteria: SLI declaration schema for endpoint+model variant published and reviewed by SRE and PM
Escrow ledger design doc with credit lifecycle (mint/borrow/repay/expire) exists in Confluence
Circuit-breaker policy that uses tenant weight to order shedding implemented in staging and validated against synthetic traffic
Automated repayment and reconciliation jobs implemented with test coverage
Runbook for on-call describing how to inspect escrow state, trigger manual repayment, and perform emergency ejection of regions
Observability: dashboards for per-tenant error-budget burn, per-route p99, and escrow balances in Grafana
steps: Draft SLI declaration schema (fields: endpoint, model_variant, metric_set, buckets, tenant_weight, quality_thresholds)
Design escrow ledger API and storage (bounded retention + append-only audit log), include idempotent operations
Define tenant weighting model (configurable: static tier or dynamic revenue-weighted) and mapping to degradation priority
Implement circuit-breaker decision function with hysteresis and cooldown windows; integrate with routing layer
Add soft-shedding handlers: cached-prefix response, quantized-variant fallback, structured partial responses
Create repayment/reconciliation job and unit/integration tests
Add telemetry hooks: per-tenant burn-rate, borrow events, repayment events, and failure modes
Run chaos tests in staging: multi-region outage simulation, sudden burst from low-priority tenant, and verify no high-priority SLO regressions
Ship to canary region with limited tenants, monitor for 72h, iterate on thresholds
Document runbook and train on-call rotation
risks: Escrow borrow logic could allow sustained borrowing without repayment leading to long-term SLO erosion
Incorrect tenant weighting may bias shed order and cause customer dissatisfaction
Complexity in cross-region reconciliation could cause transient double-counting of credits
Soft-shedding fallbacks can silently degrade quality and require eval triggers to detect regressions
Circuit-breaker thresholds tuned on synthetic workloads may not generalize to production traffic patterns
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Initial triage and scoping. Recommend tenant weighting configurable per-organization and a conservative escrow cap per tenant.
2026-03-11 Marco Liu: Architecture spike completed for ledger (append-only audit + periodic compaction). Prototype uses Bigtable with changefeed for metrics ingestion.
2026-03-12 PM review (Eleanor Cho): PM ok with prioritization rules but requests explicit UX for tenants to view escrow balance in Console
2026-03-13 Design feedback (Ravi Menon): Runbook must include explicit rollback commands and example Grafana queries. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-14 Engineering update: Implemented circuit-breaker decision function in feature branch, opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
2026-03-14 Testing note: Staging chaos test suggests borrow caps need tighter defaults (reduced from 10% to 3% of tenant daily tokens)
Next: finish repayment job, wire telemetry, and schedule canary deploy for 2026-03-18
